What the barrier establishes

The theorem concerns the cone generated by F and the acquired QC seed F+C0+4096T, with normalized positive convex combinations, translations, scalar rescaling, the specified continuous output rotations and Gamma, QC quadratic additions, affine/determinant gauges and coefficientwise limits. It is not the cone of every QC mechanism or every possible symmetry/operation.

The Bombieri cubic tensor norm is invariant under the specified orthogonal action. Projecting out translation cubics yields a positive invariant metric M on the eight charge coordinates; exact infinitesimal-rotation and Gamma identities establish the continuous symmetry claim. This is stronger than checking the earlier eight selected polynomial generators.

The key second ingredient is completed ROC slack: translation preserves it, and convex mixing adds a nonnegative variance term. The retained globally ROC1859 comparator leaves every scaled seed a positive slack of4474 lambda²|R|². Invariant-norm convexity prevents that slack disappearing while retaining C0's charge. At the exact ordinary rank-one lower witness, any generated F+C0+nu T therefore has nu at least2237+1858.795157422027..., namely4095.795157422027.... Continuity handles coefficientwise limits, including unbounded representations of a convergent polynomial. The source gives the analytic closure argument; the exact constructor checks the metric identities and literal witness, with one variance-identity diagnostic rather than claiming that one diagnostic proves the universal algebra.

Comparison and significance

The preceding orbit theorem proves all-eight-charge coverage and useful sufficient QC completions. This barrier shows that linear coverage does not make their positive closure complete: the listed operations cannot come remotely close to the1859 target. It is a meaningful limitation of a proof construction, not a QC counterexample, failure of actual-gradient capacity, or completed ROC/QC separation. The prior4096 theorem remains valid.
